definitions.explanation: A commercial establishment where customers rent a table and play mahjong, usually by the hour. They are a familiar feature of station-front buildings and of student and office-worker life.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{雀荘|じゃんそう}がある。
examples.english: There's a mahjong parlor in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {大学時代|だいがくじだい}はよく{雀荘|じゃんそう}に{通|かよ}っていた。
examples.english: In my university days I used to go to the mahjong parlor a lot.

examples.japanese: {雀荘|じゃんそう}で{朝|あさ}まで{打|う}っていたせいで、{授業|じゅぎょう}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{寝|ね}てしまった。
examples.english: Because I was playing at the mahjong parlor until morning, I slept through all my classes.

notes:
The {雀|じゃん} is from {麻雀|マージャン} (mahjong), and {荘|そう} is the same "lodge, villa" character found in apartment-building names. Note the irregular reading: {雀|じゃん} here, not すずめ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雀荘|じゃんそう}に{通|かよ}う: to frequent a mahjong parlor
- {雀荘|じゃんそう}で{打|う}つ: to play (mahjong) at a parlor — {打|う}つ is the standard verb for playing mahjong
- フリーの{雀荘|じゃんそう}: a parlor where solo customers are matched into a group

CULTURAL NOTE:
Parlors advertise themselves as ノーレート (no stakes) or by the rate played. In fiction and memoirs the {雀荘|じゃんそう} is a stock setting for all-night student life.
